turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. Estella, please.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, show this boy the way to the parlor. Let him see the place where time has stood still.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Take his hand, Estella, and lead him through the halls of my sorrow.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let him see the place where I froze time, Estella. Let him see the place where my heart stopped.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Watch him closely, Estella. Ensure he feels the weight of this place as deeply as I do.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll follow you, Miss Estella. Wherever Miss Havisham asks, I will go.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Take him to the room with the wedding cake, Estella. Let him see the taste of my bitterness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Estella, I'll see the room with the wedding cake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I await your return, Pip. Let Estella show you the remnants of my once hopeful heart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll come back soon.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Pip, what you see here is not just a room, but a chamber of secrets and sorrows.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll do my best to understand what this place means to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Indeed, Pip. You are a curious boy, and I have a feeling you will see more than you expect.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I'll try to be as attentive as I can.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, Pip, your attentiveness is commendable. Now, let us begin our little game.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll do my best to play along, if that's what you want.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, Pip. Begin by telling me what you think of my estate and my peculiar ways.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Well, Miss Havisham, your estate is very big and old, and it feels a bit lonely and... sad, I think. I've never seen anything quite like it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Lonely and sad, you say? Yes, it is a place frozen in time, much like my heart. Tell me, Pip, do you see anything unusual in this room?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
